subtitle: Conker returns with a new coat of fur

body: Conker: Live & Reloaded is Rare's Xbox remake of Conker's Bad Fur Day, released in North America on 21 June 2005. The single-player adventure revisits the squirrel's increasingly unpleasant journey with extensively rebuilt visuals and a small number of changes to enemies and equipment. Its mixture of platforming, film parody and adult comedy remains at the centre. Alongside that familiar campaign, Rare created a substantially different multiplayer game for Xbox Live, making the release both a return to the Nintendo 64 adventure and a new experiment in team-based console combat.

Multiplayer places the SHC against the Tediz, with six soldier classes offering distinct weapons, strengths and weaknesses. A sniper's range, a Sneeker's infiltration tools and a heavier soldier's durability encourage different contributions to the same objective. Terminals dispense equipment and vehicles, while upgrade orbs expand a character's capabilities until death returns the orb to the battlefield. The player has to consider what the team currently needs as well as the immediate target. Choosing a class changes which route, opponent or piece of equipment is most useful to pursue.

Rare began developing the Xbox version after Microsoft's acquisition of the studio in 2002. Robin Beanland's music and the campaign's familiar characters connect it to the earlier release, while the class-based multiplayer gives the same world a new structure. Vehicles, equipment terminals and team objectives create a broader battlefield than the original multiplayer arenas. The two halves offer distinct reasons to return: one revisits Conker's comic adventure in a more detailed presentation, while the other places his world inside the online team-play ambitions of the original Xbox era.
